Ready to start your journey at Eastern Michigan University?
Whether you're beginning your college education, pursuing an advanced degree, or getting a head start in your education, Eastern Michigan University has what you need to begin your journey toward a successful career. Here's how we can help:
First-Year Students: Build essential skills, explore careers, and access early opportunities.
Transfer Students: Transfer credits smoothly and fast-track your degree.
International Students: Earn global credentials with career support in the U.S. and abroad.
Graduate Students: Deepen expertise, lead with confidence, and pursue advanced roles.
Continuing & Adult Learners: Upskill or pivot with flexible, experience-based programs.

FAQ
Whether you're just starting out or continuing your journey, our FAQs offer quick answers and helpful guidance tailored to first-year, transfer, international, graduate, and adult learners—including important information about application deadlines to help you stay on track.

Undergraduate Application Deadlines
Expand dropdown
Undergraduate Priority Deadlines
EMU accepts applications for admission on a rolling basis throughout the year. However, it’s best to apply as early as possible, up to 15 months prior to your intended start date.
A priority admission deadline is the last day completed application files must be submitted in order to be admitted in time for the start of your intended semester.
The following guidelines provide information about how the timing of your application may affect your consideration for admission and/or financial aid:
Domestic students should apply by:
July 1 for programs beginning in Fall
November 1 for programs beginning in Winter
April 1 for programs beginning in Summer
International students should apply by:
June 24, 2025 for Fall 2025
November 4, 2025 for Winter 2026
Applicants who are not U.S. citizens or who have transcripts from outside the United States are subject to the deadlines for international students. International applicants who need an I-20 should apply as early as possible.
Graduate Application Deadlines
Expand dropdown
Graduate Priority Deadlines
We strongly recommend all applicants submit application materials before the priority dates listed below. The priority dates allow for expedited application review and may include opportunities for the admitted student to apply for graduate assistantships and graduate school scholarships. International applicants who need an I-20 should always apply as early as possible
May 1 for enrollment beginning in Fall
October 1 for enrollment beginning in Winter
March 1 for enrollment beginning in Summer
If you have questions about the graduate application process or your graduate application status, please contact the Office of Admissions at graduate_admissions@emich.edu or 734.487.3060. Additionally, please contact the graduate program's department for specific program questions
Graduate Programs With Fixed Deadlines
Some graduate programs require applicants to submit all application materials by a posted deadline. Some graduate programs admit students one time each year. Please consult the program information in the Graduate Catalog or contact the appropriate academic department to determine if your program has a specific application deadline.
Rolling Graduate Admissions
Many graduate programs offer rolling admissions processes and continue to accept applicants right up until the start of the semester or until all seats are filled. Admitted graduate students must enroll in a course during the semester selected on their application for admission.
Fall Semester: Typically runs from September through mid-December
Winter Semester: Typically runs from January through mid-April
Summer Semester: Typically runs from May through mid-August
To assist you with your planning, view detailed academic calendars.

Undergraduate Financial Aid Deadlines
Expand dropdown
Undergraduate Priority Deadlines
Entering freshmen and transfer students are automatically considered for academic scholarships at the time of admission, based on availability of funds. In addition, students who have submitted FAFSA information are automatically considered for federal financial aid and/or additional grants.
For priority scholarship and financial aid consideration, EMU strongly recommends that students submit completed admission and the FAFSA (Free Application for Federal Student Aid) by the following dates:
Incoming Freshmen:
March 15 for programs beginning in Fall
Incoming Transfer:
March 15 for programs beginning in Fall
Graduate Financial Aid Deadlines
Expand dropdown
Graduate Scholarship and Fellowship Priority Deadlines*
June 15
*For consideration for EMU Graduate School scholarships and fellowships, you must be admitted to EMU and have submitted your graduate financial assistance application form.
How can I apply to Eastern Michigan University (EMU)?
Expand dropdown
You can start your application to Eastern Michigan University by selecting “Undergraduate” in the dropdown menu at the top of the page and then choose your desired start term. You can also apply by using the Common App.
When do admissions decisions for undergraduate applicants typically come out?
Expand dropdown
EMU offers rolling admissions and will begin administering decisions for 2026 undergraduate applicants starting in October 2025. Most admissions decisions are made within 3-14 business days after all required materials are received.
Does EMU accept applications on a rolling basis?
Expand dropdown
Yes, while applying early is encouraged, EMU does accept undergraduate applications on a rolling basis throughout the year.
Are standardized tests (SAT/ACT) required for admission?
Expand dropdown
Eastern Michigan University offers a test-optional admission option, providing flexibility for applicants.
What information is available regarding costs and scholarships?
Expand dropdown
The university provides generous scholarship opportunities for undergraduate students. You can view scholarship information here. For more information on costs, you can visit the financial aid webpage
How can I get more information about specific programs or opportunities?
Expand dropdown
You can request more information about specific programs and opportunities by filling out our Request for Information form.
Who can I contact for personalized guidance on becoming an EMU Eagle?
Expand dropdown
You can contact our admissions office by phone at 734.487.6453 or by email at undergraduate_admissions@emich.edu. You can also reach out to your designated admissions counselor here.
What are the admission requirements for transfer students?
Expand dropdown
All students wishing to transfer to EMU must have a cumulative college grade point average (GPA) of 2.0 or above and 12 or more transferable credits earned. You can view more details about our admission requirements here.
How does Eastern Michigan University handle transfer credits?
Expand dropdown
EMU awards transfer credit for courses taken at regionally accredited colleges or universities, in which the student earned a grade of "C" (2.0 on a 4 point scale) or above. Find more details about our transfer credit policy.
What is the application process for transfer students?
Expand dropdown
Prospective transfer students are encouraged to begin an application by following the dropdown menu at the top of this page. Select your student type (Undergraduate or Graduate) and your desired start term to get started.
Does EMU have agreements with other institutions for transferring credits?
Expand dropdown
Yes, Eastern Michigan University utilizes transfer tools such as articulation agreements to facilitate the transfer process. You can learn more about our articulation agreements here.
Where can I get personalized guidance or answers to my questions about transferring to EMU?
Expand dropdown
You can contact our admissions office by phone at 734.487.6453 or by email at transfer_admissions@emich.edu. You can also reach out to your designated transfer admissions counselor here.
Does Eastern Michigan University accept international students?
Expand dropdown
Yes, Eastern Michigan University welcomes international students for both undergraduate and graduate programs, offering a variety of academic opportunities.
What is unique about the campus environment for international students?
Expand dropdown
EMU provides a dynamic campus community located conveniently 25 minutes from Detroit International Airport, featuring small class sizes, dynamic faculty, and excellent campus facilities.
Are there specific tuition or scholarship benefits for international students?
Expand dropdown
There is no out-of-state tuition for undergraduate international students, and significant scholarship opportunities are available for graduate international students. More information about costs and scholarship opportunities for international students can be found here.
What kind of support services are available for international students?
Expand dropdown
International students receive support from both the Office for International Students and Scholars (OISS) and the English as a Second Language (ESL) program.
How can I contact the International Admissions office for more information?
Expand dropdown
You can reach the International Admissions office by phone at +1.734.487.0205 or by email at international_admissions@emich.edu. You can also find your designated International Admissions Counselor here.
How do I complete an application that I previously started?
Expand dropdown
Please choose a program and term and click the apply button to go to the proper application system. If you already have a login ID and PIN, please use them to finish the application. If you no longer have the login credentials, please use the reset password functions within the application system to retrieve your login credentials. If you are using CAS to apply, please contact CAS support for login issues.
Where do I send my transcripts?
Expand dropdown
Applicants will follow instructions within CAS to request transcripts from previously attended schools.
How do I follow the progress of my submitted application?
Expand dropdown
If you have already submitted your application, you will be able to follow its progress through the Graduate Admissions review system. Each time you login to your portal using your Login ID and PIN, you will find a brief admissions progress Display Code. Review a full explanation of the meaning of each Display Code [PDF]. Please refer to the EMU Academic Catalog for all admissions requirements for the program you applied to. You will be notified through email if you have outstanding items. Once a decision is made, you will be notified through email of the decision. Please make sure you add graduate_admissions@emich.edu to your contact list to receive all communications.
Can I submit applications to more than one EMU graduate program?
Expand dropdown
Yes. Moreover, you are permitted to apply for admission to all such programs in the same semester, or you can apply for admission to different programs in different semesters.
Can I use the same application materials to apply to a second EMU graduate program?
Expand dropdown
Different programs may require different application materials. Please refer to the EMU Academic Catalog for detailed admissions requirements for the program you are interested in. In many cases, if you apply to a different term, updated materials are needed to reflect the most up-to-date information. If you apply to the same term, transcripts and evaluations can be shared. You will need to send in new copies for other required materials.
What if I submit my application and later change my mind about the semester in which I would like to start my graduate studies?
Expand dropdown
Don’t worry. We will always permit you to update your application materials to reflect the semester that you desire within a two year cycle from the original application date. Please fill out the Graduate Admission Update Form [PDF] and send it back to us. If you would like to change to a semester outside of the application cycle, please submit a new application. Please contact graduate_admissions@emich.edu for assistance.
Who do I contact with questions about the application process and/or the status of my application?
Expand dropdown
If you have questions about the application process or your application status, please contact the Office of Admissions at graduate_admissions@emich.edu or 734.487.3060.
Who do I contact about program-specific questions?
Expand dropdown
Please contact the graduate program's department for specific program questions. The program’s department is listed with the program information in the EMU Academic Catalog.
How do I change to a different major?
Expand dropdown
A new application is necessary and please also check the graduate catalog for specific program information including start dates, deadlines and required application documents. https://catalog.emich.edu
What if I have not registered for classes in the past two years?
Expand dropdown
Graduate students must submit a new application and pay the application fee to reapply.
Does Eastern Michigan University support students returning after a break to complete their degree?
Expand dropdown
Yes, if you're looking to complete your degree after a break from classes, Eastern Michigan University can help guide you through the re-enrollment process. Reach out to an admissions counselor or visit this webpage for more information.
Does Eastern Michigan University offer a Post-Bachelor degree program?
Expand dropdown
Yes, Eastern Michigan University provides a Post-Bachelor degree program. A Post-Bachelor degree program is ideal for individuals with an existing bachelor's degree who need additional undergraduate coursework to meet prerequisites for graduate school, are seeking a second bachelor's degree, or are specifically aiming for teacher certification in Elementary or Secondary Education. For admissions requirements, click here.
Who is considered a guest student at Eastern Michigan University?
Expand dropdown
Guest students are undergraduate students who are currently enrolled or actively pursuing a degree at another college or university but wish to take classes at EMU with the intent to transfer credit back to their home institution. Admissions requirements to become a guest student can be found here.
What is dual enrollment at Eastern Michigan University, and who is eligible?
Expand dropdown
Dual enrollment allows public and charter high school students with demonstrated academic potential to take college-level courses at EMU, enriching their high school experience with courses they might not otherwise have access to. Eligible students must have a cumulative high school GPA of 2.5 or higher. More information on dual enrollment can be found here.
Are there specific programs or opportunities for senior learners?
Expand dropdown
Yes, Senior Learning Opportunities at Eastern Michigan University provide Michigan residents age 62 and above the option to audit classes, pending instructor approval. To learn more, visit this webpage.
Where can I get more information or assistance with continuing my education?
Expand dropdown
You can contact the Office of Admissions at 734.487.6453 or by email at undergraduate_admissions@emich.edu ortransfer_admissions@emich.edu. You can also contact a specific admissions counselor here.
CONTACT INFORMATION
Embarking on the journey of higher education is an exciting step, and we're here to guide you through every stage of the admissions process. Reach out to us for personalized guidance, detailed information on programs, and answers to all your questions on becoming an EMU Eagle.
